1.name: Tropical rainforest
1.description: Hot temperatures in every month with abundant rainfall and no dry season. Forest cover is supported by consistently wet conditions.
1.examples: Amazon basin, Congo basin, Indonesia, Malaysia, southern India

2.name: Tropical monsoon
2.description: Hot year-round with a short dry season and very heavy seasonal rains. Rainfall is strongly shaped by monsoon circulation.
2.examples: Western India, Bangladesh, coastal Myanmar, southern Vietnam, West Africa

3.name: Tropical savanna
3.description: Hot in all months with a pronounced winter dry season and a wetter summer. Seasonal rainfall often supports grasslands and open woodland.
3.examples: East Africa, central Brazil, northern Australia, Llanos of Venezuela and Colombia

4.name: Hot desert
4.description: Annual precipitation is far below the dry-climate threshold, with mean annual temperature above 18 C. Extreme aridity and high heat dominate.
4.examples: Sahara, Arabian Peninsula, central Australia, SW United States

5.name: Cold desert
5.description: Very low annual precipitation with a mean annual temperature below 18 C. Winters can be cold despite persistently dry conditions.
5.examples: Gobi Desert, Great Basin, Patagonian Desert, Taklamakan Desert

6.name: Hot semi-arid
6.description: Dry climate near the desert threshold with mean annual temperature above 18 C. Rainfall is limited but generally enough to support grassland or scrub.
6.examples: Sahel, Deccan Plateau, NE Brazil, northern Mexico, parts of Australia

7.name: Cold semi-arid
7.description: Dry steppe climate with mean annual temperature below 18 C. Large seasonal temperature ranges are common.
7.examples: Central Asia, US High Plains, interior Spain, Patagonia, Mongolia

8.name: Hot-summer Mediterranean
8.description: Mild, wetter winters and hot, dry summers. Summer drought is strong and shapes vegetation and water demand.
8.examples: Mediterranean Basin, California valleys, central Chile, SW Australia

9.name: Warm-summer Mediterranean
9.description: Mild, wet winters and warm, dry summers moderated by latitude, elevation, or ocean influence. Summer drought is present but heat is less intense than Csa.
9.examples: Coastal California, Pacific Northwest uplands, northern Portugal, parts of Chile

10.name: Cold-summer Mediterranean
10.description: A rare dry-summer temperate climate with cool summers and mild to cool winters. It usually occurs in exposed coastal or high-elevation settings.
10.examples: Coastal Iceland margins, Faroe Islands uplands, high Andes, small Pacific Northwest areas

11.name: Monsoon-influenced humid subtropical
11.description: Hot summers, mild winters, and a distinct winter dry season. Most precipitation falls during the warm season.
11.examples: Northern India, southern China interior, northern Vietnam, parts of Paraguay

12.name: Subtropical highland
12.description: Mild to warm summers, cool winters, and a dry winter season. Elevation commonly moderates temperatures in otherwise tropical or subtropical regions.
12.examples: Ethiopian Highlands, Mexican Plateau, Andes valleys, Yunnan, southern Africa highlands

13.name: Cold subtropical highland
13.description: Cool summers, cold winters, and a dry winter season. This rare climate is usually confined to high mountain terrain.
13.examples: High Andes, Tibetan Plateau margins, isolated East African highlands

14.name: Humid subtropical
14.description: Hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters with significant precipitation year-round. There is no pronounced dry season.
14.examples: SE United States, eastern China, southern Brazil, eastern Argentina, NE India

15.name: Temperate oceanic
15.description: Mild winters, warm but not hot summers, and rainfall spread through the year. Marine influence often keeps temperature extremes modest.
15.examples: British Isles, western France, New Zealand, southern Chile, Pacific Northwest coast

16.name: Subpolar oceanic
16.description: Cool summers, mild to cold winters, and frequent precipitation in all seasons. It is common on high-latitude coasts exposed to ocean air.
16.examples: Faroe Islands, coastal Iceland, southern Alaska coast, Tierra del Fuego

17.name: Hot-summer continental Mediterranean
17.description: Hot, dry summers and cold winters with a strong continental temperature range. It is usually found inland from Mediterranean regions.
17.examples: Interior Turkey, Iranian Plateau, inland western United States, parts of Central Asia

18.name: Warm-summer continental Mediterranean
18.description: Warm, dry summers and snowy or cold winters. Elevation or latitude keeps summer heat below the hot-summer subtype.
18.examples: Rocky Mountains, Sierra Nevada, eastern Turkey highlands, parts of Iran

19.name: Cold-summer continental Mediterranean
19.description: Short, cool, dry summers and long cold winters. This rare subtype is mostly found in high mountains near dry-summer climates.
19.examples: High Sierra Nevada, high Rockies, highlands of eastern Turkey and Iran

20.name: Very-cold continental Mediterranean
20.description: Dry summers combine with extremely cold winters. It is one of the rarest Koppen-Geiger classes and is mostly tied to severe high-elevation interiors.
20.examples: High mountain interiors of eastern Siberia and Central Asia

21.name: Hot-summer monsoon continental
21.description: Hot summers, very cold winters, and a pronounced winter dry season. Most precipitation arrives in the warm season.
21.examples: Northeastern China, Korean Peninsula interior, Russian Far East margins

22.name: Warm-summer monsoon continental
22.description: Warm summers, cold winters, and dry winters. It often appears in uplands or higher-latitude monsoon-influenced interiors.
22.examples: Northeastern China uplands, North Korea highlands, parts of Siberia and Mongolia

23.name: Subarctic monsoon
23.description: Short, cool summers and long cold winters with a strong winter dry season. It is common in severe continental interiors influenced by seasonal pressure systems.
23.examples: Eastern Siberia, Russian Far East interior, northern Mongolia

24.name: Extreme subarctic monsoon
24.description: Very long, intensely cold winters and brief cool summers, with winters also being dry. This is among the coldest inhabited climate settings.
24.examples: Yakutia, Verkhoyansk region, Oymyakon region, interior eastern Siberia

25.name: Hot-summer humid continental
25.description: Hot summers, cold winters, and precipitation in all seasons. Seasonal contrasts are strong, with both summer heat and winter freezes.
25.examples: US Midwest, lower Great Lakes, Balkans, Ukraine, NE China margins

26.name: Warm-summer humid continental
26.description: Warm summers, cold winters, and year-round precipitation. Snow is common in winter and summers are moderate rather than hot.
26.examples: Southern Canada, northern US, central Europe, southern Scandinavia, western Russia

27.name: Subarctic
27.description: Long, cold winters and short, cool summers with precipitation in all seasons. Forests and boreal landscapes commonly dominate.
27.examples: Interior Alaska, Canada boreal forest, Scandinavia interior, Siberia

28.name: Extreme subarctic
28.groupDescription: No dry season, very cold winter
28.description: Extremely cold winters, short cool summers, and no dry season. It is concentrated in the harshest continental interiors.
28.examples: Eastern Siberia, Yakutia, high-latitude interior Russia

29.name: Tundra
29.description: The warmest month stays above 0 C but below 10 C, limiting tree growth. Vegetation is dominated by tundra, mosses, lichens, and low shrubs.
29.examples: Arctic coastlines, Greenland margins, Antarctic Peninsula, high alpine zones

30.name: Ice cap
30.description: All months average below 0 C, so permanent ice or snow can persist. Liquid-water growing seasons are effectively absent.
30.examples: Interior Greenland, Antarctica, highest Himalayan and Andean ice fields
